feature: The walks that were failing in the sweep
summary: Six scripted walks the last sweep reported broken pass again. Two were the app driving itself wrong (Escape did not put a popover away, and a key aimed at the whole app needed a document open), and four were walks still asking for things the app moved on from.
setup: Nothing to turn on. These are the app's own scripted walks, run against the probe build: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/<name>.json --no-build, about ten seconds each. The Mac's screen was locked for all of this, so every picture here is the real window taken under a lock.

try.do: Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/corner-drag-rounds-walk.json --no-build and watch it go green.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: In the app, pick a box, open the four corner numbers with the chevron beside Corner Radius, and press Escape. The popout goes away.

try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Read the Outline row in that picture: Mixed, and under it one plain line saying 1 of the 3 selected layers has an outline.
Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/icon-stroke-weight-walk.json --no-build: a line drawn on a 24 pixel icon frame arrives 2 points thick, and the same line on a Desktop frame arrives at 4.
Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/never-granting-walk.json --no-build, the first run of a walk written on 2026-09-16 that had never once been executed.

evaluate: Pressing Escape over an open popout: does it put the popout away for you every time, or is there a case where it takes the whole selection with it?

switch-says-mixed now asks its question of three closed paths rather than three boxes, because a box arrives with no line any more. Is a path still a fair stand-in for what you would actually be doing?

A box drawn on a 24 pixel icon frame arrives with no edge at all, so there is no weight for the frame to decide. Is arriving bare still what you want on an icon, where a line is usually the whole drawing?
Is a walk that reads the picture's row after clicking it still proving what you wanted proved, or does the row needing a click say something is wrong with where that count lives?
rough: A border ADDED from the plus arrives at 2 points whatever the frame is. On a 24 pixel icon that is exactly the weight a drawn line gets, so it looks right; on a 16 pixel one a drawn line would be 1 and the added border is 2. Too small to file, and written into the task log instead.

switch-says-mixed lost the case it was written for: three boxes disagreeing about a border. That case now needs the plus menu, and a menu cannot be opened while the screen is locked, so the walk would have stopped running altogether. Paths keep it running and test the same rule.

Twelve of the walks that press Escape over a popout could not be re-run at all: they look a control up by name and the screen is locked. They will be covered by the next full sweep on an unlocked Mac.
